items.text: Liverpool are now without a win in five successive Premier League home games (D4 L1) after the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City, BBC Sport reports, with Andoni Iraola saying his side played "two different games" either side of the red card. Small Ben owns Virgil, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Isak, Big Ben has Wirtz, Justin has Barcola and Marcus has Becker.

source.title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?

items.text: Small Ben named his team Delap Dance, and Delap is on Big Ben's squad, where he returned 2 in GW6. Small Ben sits on 281, 45 behind Marcus, with Virgil, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Isak all showing 0 on his squad sheet. It is a team named after a man he does not own, held together by four Liverpool players who did nothing.

Justin is on 290, 36 behind Marcus, and left 7 points on his bench in GW6 while Haaland returned 6. His bench has therefore out-scored his centre-forward, which is the sort of thing a man with a team called Schwaddy should have noticed before Wednesday night.

Robert is on 205, which is 121 behind Marcus and the best part of a whole other league away. Mateta, Sesko, James and Mosquera all show 0 for GW6 on his squad sheet, so at least the zeros have each other for company. The only good news is that none of GW7's ten fixtures has kicked off yet, so he has a full eleven still to disappoint us with.

Brighton's Pascal Struijk has had his red card at Sunderland overturned on appeal, BBC Sport reports, so he dodges the one-match ban and is available for the visit of Crystal Palace this weekend. He was sent off after 57 minutes on a VAR call for denying Wilson Isidor, and Brighton still won 2-0. Marcus (De Cuyper, Kostoulas), Justin (Vuskovic) and Big Ben (Gross) all own Brighton players and keep their defence at full strength for GW7.

source.title: Struijk red card after VAR intervention overturned

items.text: BBC Sport argues the three-week break did Chelsea more good than anyone: Xabi Alonso reworked a back three that had shipped a league-high 12 goals before the pause, Moises Caicedo returned from his calf problem, and the 5-1 win over Bournemouth followed. Joao Pedro, who scored twice, said the break gave them time to fix the mistakes from the 3-0 loss at Brentford. Edward owns Palmer, Marcus has Joao Pedro and Big Ben has Rogers, and Chelsea go to Everton at 11:30 on Saturday.

source.title: Did Chelsea benefit most from extended international break?

items.text: Lisandro Martinez publicly questioned Manchester United's summer recruitment after the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, telling CBS "we don't have the best squad at the moment compared to other top teams" and "I expect more from our technical director", BBC Sport reports. Director of football Jason Wilcox is the target again. Robert (Yoro, Sesko), Marcus (Mbeumo), Small Ben (Cunha) and Big Ben (Bruno Fernandes) all have United players, and United are at Leeds on Saturday.

source.title: Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout

items.text: Marcus started GW6 ten points behind Edward and finished it 28 clear, a 38-point swing built on 77 to Edward's 39. De Cuyper 15, Dewsbury-Hall 13 and Joao Pedro 12 supplied 40 of them, and a left-back on 15 is the sort of thing people call luck right up until he is in their own team.

Robert was 89 behind the leader when GW6 began and is 121 behind now, having scored 35, exactly what Small Ben and Big Ben scored. Thirty-two points of ground gone in a week on a perfectly respectable return is the first thing to recede that fast in that part of the league since his hairline.

Small Ben began GW6 13 points off the top and ended it 45 off, with Cunha on 10, Donnarumma on 9 and Rice on 7 not nearly enough to stop it. For a man who is always looking up at somebody, the leader is now a very long way up.

Lisandro Martinez has apologised and been fined by Manchester United after criticising the club's hierarchy following the Atletico Madrid defeat, BBC Sport reports. He met the club's leadership and Michael Carrick on Thursday and said he spoke out of frustration. It remains to be seen whether Carrick picks him for Leeds on Sunday at 14:00 BST. Robert has Yoro, Ben D has Bruno Fernandes, Small Ben has Cunha and Marcus has Mbeumo, so four of the six have a stake in how this dressing room feels.

source.title: Martinez apologises for outburst and fined by Man Utd

items.text: The Guardian's weekend preview picks out Jordan Henderson, who at 36 became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game against Bournemouth, as the man who may dictate Chelsea's trip to unbeaten Everton. His partnership with Moises Caicedo is what lets Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer flourish: Rogers is Big Ben's, Joao Pedro is Marcus's and Palmer is Edward's. Everton's defence, in the Guardian's words, littered the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, and Tarkowski, Branthwaite and Pickford belong to Edward, Big Ben and Justin.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Gonzalo Garcia has one league goal from 18 shots this season and has not scored since his debut against Chelsea, the Guardian notes ahead of bottom club Fulham hosting Hull City. Fulham have six goals in six games and head coach Alvaro Arbeloa is under increasing pressure. Garcia is Big Ben's, and on the Guardian's numbers his expected goals tally of 3.60 says the finishing is due to turn.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Small Ben cut Gakpo for Anderson of Man City in the latest waivers, and Gakpo is now flagged at 25% to play, so the timing was perfect for once. The trouble is Isak and Szoboszlai, still his, both flagged at 25% and both on 0 in GW6 alongside Virgil. He got rid of the one Liverpool player who was no use to him and kept the two who may not be fit, which is a long way from the training camp a man with a boxing match coming should be running.

Justin dropped Strand Larsen a week after he returned 5, signed Brobbey of Sunderland, and then dropped E.Le Fee of Sunderland for Stach of Leeds, so he has swapped one Sunderland player for another and called it a plan. Ajayi went for Bogle, also Leeds. Three claims, no recognisable name in any of them, from a manager who left 7 points on his bench in GW6 and decided the fix was at the other end of the pitch.

Big Ben left 12 points on his bench in GW6, the most in the league and a third of what his eleven managed (35). Robert left 1. His Arsenal are Konsa on 4 and Havertz on 2, fewer than Edward or Robert hold, which is a thin return for the league's loudest Arsenal voice. Thiaw, who returned 0, went out for Ajer of Brentford in the waivers, so at least the bench is learning to rotate.

Marcus scored 77 in GW6 and 40 of it came from De Cuyper 15, Dewsbury-Hall 13 and Joao Pedro 12: a Brighton left-back, an Everton midfielder and a Chelsea forward, none of whom anyone else would have named. He leads Edward by 28 with Foden and Tzolis both on 0. Anybody can call that luck, but a man who has been on the right side of it three weeks running is just a different kind of planner.

Reece James is out for around three months after knee surgery, BBC Sport reports, the problem picked up in training before Chelsea's 5-1 win over Bournemouth. Xabi Alonso says it is not a two or three week job and expects him back before January. James sits in Robert's squad, which had a quiet Gameweek 6 to forget and now has a Chelsea defender to carry through to Christmas.

source.title: Chelsea's James out for three months after knee surgery

items.text: Chelsea go to Everton at 12.30 today without Emmanuel Emegha, still waiting on his debut, with Alonso confirming he is not fit enough for the trip. The Chelsea players the league holds are Joao Pedro and Palestra for Marcus, Palmer for Edward, Rogers for Big Ben and Estevao for Robert, and they meet an Everton that has Dewsbury-Hall for Marcus and Tarkowski, Garner and Barry for Edward.

source.title: Chelsea's James out for three months after knee surgery

items.text: Brighton's Pascal Struijk has had his red card at Sunderland overturned on appeal, BBC Sport reports, so he avoids the one-match ban and is available for the trip to Crystal Palace this weekend. Brighton are third, five points behind Manchester City. Marcus has De Cuyper and Kostoulas there, Justin has Vuskovic and Big Ben has Gross, with Palace's Strand Larsen, Khalaili and Mateta on the other side of the derby for Justin, Edward and Robert.

source.title: Struijk red card shown after VAR intervention is overturned

items.text: Team news, Everton v Chelsea (11:30 UTC). Chelsea sheet confirmed. Marcus: Joao Pedro starts, Palestra on the bench. Edward: Palmer starts. Big Ben: Rogers starts. Robert: Martinez starts, Estevao on the bench, James not in the squad. Everton's eleven was not available at a permitted outlet, so Dewsbury-Hall, Tarkowski, Barry, Pickford and Branthwaite are left out of this report.

source.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Everton

items.text: Team news, 15:00 kick-offs: Liverpool's confirmed XI at Brentford has all six league players starting - Marcus (Alisson), Small Ben (Van Dijk, Szoboszlai, Isak), Big Ben (Wirtz) and Justin (Barcola). Teamsheets for Brentford, Fulham and Man City were not available at time of writing, so league players at those clubs are not counted yet.

source.title: Team news: Confirmed Liverpool line-up v Brentford

items.text: Team news, Newcastle v Aston Villa (17:30 BST): Newcastle's confirmed XI is out. Edward's Horníček starts in goal; Small Ben's Hall and Wissa both start. Aston Villa's confirmed XI was not available when checked, so Edward's Manzambi and N.Jackson and Small Ben's Suzuki are not counted either way.

source.title: Confirmed line-up: Joelinton in for first start of season

items.text: Marcus went into the weekend 28 ahead of Edward and 36 ahead of Justin. Tonight it is 13 and 19: Edward has 24 so far on Manzambi's 11 and Leno's 6, Justin has 26 on Haaland's 13 and Lewis-Potter's 9, and Marcus has 9 from five players on 1 or 2 each, with Foden's 9 sitting on his bench. Six of his eleven have not played, against seven of Justin's and four of Edward's, so the lead is still his but the rest of the gameweek will decide how much of it survives.

Small Ben has 12 in his eleven and 22 on his bench. Isak 9, Suzuki 8, Hall 4 and Szoboszlai 1 watched from the sideline while Donnarumma, Ruben and Anderson took a point each for Man City, and he is 42 behind Marcus with five of his eleven still to play. If he reads a boxing ring the way he reads a team sheet, whoever is standing across from him should plan on an early night.

Big Ben named his team Quantum of Tzolis, and Tzolis is on Marcus's squad, on 0, not yet played. Big Ben himself is 63 behind the man who owns his namesake, with 18 so far from Affengruber's 6 and Wirtz's 5. Bruno, Konsa and Havertz are all still to play, so the question is not whether the rest of his weekend is a bailout but which of the three gets to be the one he waits on.

Robert has 15 on the day and 13 of it is Martinez 8 and Ndiaye 5. Two of his eleven have played and returned nothing, six have not kicked off, and he is 115 behind Marcus, which makes first place the only thing in his life receding faster than his hairline. There is still time for him to get closer, which is the sort of thing he says before every gameweek.

Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 on Saturday but lost Robert's Martinez for the afternoon: the goalkeeper was carried off with his neck in a brace after a collision with Big Ben's Branthwaite and taken to hospital with suspected concussion, the Guardian reports. Alonso said only that Martinez was conscious leaving the ground and the club need to wait. Robert has no other goalkeeper on his squad but Roefs, and Chelsea's next fixture will say whether he has a decision to make.

source.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martinez head injury

items.text: Liverpool came from behind to win 2-1 at Brentford once Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for a headbutt on Jacquet, with Isak scoring the 70th-minute winner from Barcola's header, the Guardian reports. That is Small Ben's Isak and Justin's Barcola on the same goal, and Big Ben's Wirtz supplied the pass for Munoz's equaliser. Small Ben also lost Szoboszlai to injury in the first half, and Brentford ended with nine after Janelt's second yellow, which Big Ben (Kelleher, Ajer) and Justin (Lewis-Potter, Schade) will be reading with interest.

source.title: Isak completes Liverpool's comeback win as Brentford finish with nine

items.text: Johan Manzambi headed Aston Villa in front on 36 minutes at Newcastle, ghosting away from Thiaw to meet Joao Gomes's cross, and that was the only goal, the Guardian reports. It was Edward's Manzambi doing it to Edward's own goalkeeper Hornicek, who was also bailed out when a Buendia shot hit the post and deflected off his back before Small Ben's Hall cleared; the report calls Hall Newcastle's best player again.

source.title: Manzambi maintains Aston Villa progress with win to seal dismal week for Newcastle

items.text: Everton lost for the first time this season, and Justin's Pickford was unconvincing for a second week running: Neto scored 44 seconds after the restart, beating Pickford low to his left with a shot the Guardian calls a weak attempt to save, the ball having taken a touch off Edward's Tarkowski on the way. Big Ben's Rogers survived a second-yellow challenge on Garner just before half-time for Chelsea.

source.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martinez head injury

items.text: Team news, 13:00 UTC kick-offs: Crystal Palace's confirmed eleven is out and Mateta (Robert) is on the bench, not starting at Brighton. Teamsheets for Bournemouth v Sunderland, Brighton and Leeds v Man Utd were not available at a permitted source, so Tavernier, Truffert, Silva, Evanilson, Brobbey, Roefs, Mukiele, Vuskovic, Gross, Kadioglu, De Cuyper, Kostoulas, Bogle, Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Trafford, Wilson, Fernandes, Yoro, Seško, Cunha and Mbeumo are not counted.

source.title: Team news: Sage makes three changes; Mateta returns

items.text: Small Ben named his team Delap Dance and owns nobody called Delap: that Delap is Big Ben's, in the last slot of his squad, on 0. What Small Ben does own is Isak, who scored Liverpool's 70th-minute winner at Brentford and then took his 9 points to the bench, where Suzuki was already sitting on 8. Those two have 17 between them. The eleven Small Ben actually picked has 12, with five of them still to play.

Marcus leads by 13 on a day when his eleven has 9 points and his bench has 10, because Foden's 9 for Man City are sitting in a bench slot while Becker, Dewsbury-Hall, King and Joao Pedro are on 2 each. Six of his eleven have not kicked off, so he has not wrecked anything yet. But a man in front of the whole league with his best player of the day on the bench is the nearest thing to proof that it is luck.

Justin had the biggest gameweek of the six, 60 to Marcus's 56, and it cut the gap to the top from 36 to 32. Haaland 13, Vuskovic 11, Tavernier 10, Raya 9 and Lewis-Potter 9 is 52 of it. Marcus got 12 each from Kostoulas and Evanilson and has nobody left to play, so Justin's only road is two of his eleven and Tottenham v Coventry at 19:00. Everybody else lost ground to Marcus too: Edward started the weekend 28 behind and is 41 behind.

Big Ben owned Havertz and Delap, so he had a man on each side of Forest v Arsenal and took 4 points off 155 minutes of them. Konsa's 9 kept it respectable, and he is still 91 behind Marcus after starting the weekend 72 back. The league calls him an Arsenal fan with no ball knowledge to speak of, and picking both strikers from the one game for 2 points each is at least consistent.

Robert took 27 from the weekend, 16 of it from Martinez and Gabriel on 8 each, and five of his eleven played and returned nothing. Marcus took 56, so the gap to first went from 121 to 150 in one gameweek. A number like 150 is usually the sort of thing a man mentions in the group chat, and Robert, who has never been known to reply to it, will let it speak for itself.

Small Ben owns three Manchester City players and all three returned a point: Donnarumma 1, Ruben 1, Anderson 1. Haaland's 13 went to Justin and Foden's 9 went to Marcus's bench, so the City points were there and he picked up the wrong ones. He has 34 for the gameweek with one of his eleven still to play, and he is 67 behind Marcus after starting 45 back.

Evanilson had a hand in both Bournemouth goals against Sunderland: he squared for Tavernier to head the first rather than shoot, then won the red card when Danso fouled him in the 17th minute, then sat Roefs down for the second, the Guardian reports. Marcus has the man who did it, Justin has the header, and Robert has the goalkeeper. Brobbey, Justin's, was left out of the Sunderland squad altogether, Le Bris saying they decided not to rush the process after his injury on international duty.

source.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland

items.text: Brighton beat Crystal Palace 5-0 and Marcus had two in it: Kostoulas scored the fourth after setting up Ayari for the third, the Guardian reports. Big Ben's Gross started it all, his free-kick headed past Benitez by Palace's own Canvot inside the first ten minutes, and Diego Gomez's 51-metre strike made it 2-0 before Palace were three down. Pierre Sage said his feeling after the game was shame, and the report notes two of his predecessors lost their jobs not long after losing to Brighton.

source.title: Gomez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton's 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace

items.text: Manchester United's seventh league game brought a seventh point from a draw, Mbeumo's first-half opener cancelled out at Elland Road by Calvert-Lewin, who outmuscled Mbeumo at a corner for his fifth goal in ten Leeds outings, the Guardian reports. That is Edward's striker scoring against Marcus's winger. Bogle's cross and Stach's free-kick, both Justin's, supplied Leeds's best moments, and Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes was booked while playing as a nominal centre-forward in Carrick's 3-4-3.

source.title: Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin's Leeds leveller keeps pressure on Carrick

items.text: Arsenal won 1-0 at Nottingham Forest through Madueke's 80th-minute shot, deflected off Cunha after a pass from Rice, the Guardian reports, and it was Small Ben's Rice who made it. Big Ben had both sides of the late drama: his Delap was a full-throttle presence for Forest, whose manager Glasner is still waiting for a home goal this season, and his Konsa made the thunderous block that denied Delap at the death. Arsenal managed one shot on target all game.

source.title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest's resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory

items.text: Team news, Tottenham v Coventry (19:00 UTC): Justin has Van Hecke and Marmoush both starting. Marcus's Kinsky starts in goal. Robert's Solanke starts. Small Ben's Savio is out injured and not in the matchday squad. Nobody in the league owns a Coventry player.

source.title: Confirmed line-ups: Spurs vs Coventry

items.text: Justin put 73 on the board, with Haaland's 13 sitting on top of it, and took Marcus's lead down to 19. The injury feed is still calling Haaland a doubt, so the best night anybody has had all season rests on a man the league's own list says might not have been there. Second place has never sounded so much like a personality, and the Tuesday messages are already being drafted.

Kostoulas and Evanilson scored 12 apiece, which is 24 of Marcus's 56 from two players he cannot honestly say he planned around, and the lead still lost ground. It is the shape of a week where a man calls it process and everybody else calls it the usual. Kinsky stood in goal for the full 90 minutes and returned two, so the luck had a limit, and Justin found it.

Robert started Mateta, Wilson and Estevao and got one point between the three of them, while Solanke and Yoro scored four each on his bench. Sesko is injured until the end of the month and contributed exactly what an injured man contributes. The gap to Marcus is 150 now, and it is receding faster than anything on Robert's head, which is saying something.

Big Ben, Arsenal to the bone, owns Konsa and Havertz and was still passed tonight by Small Ben, whose eleven gave Cunha, Wissa and Anderson a point each while Isak and Suzuki, 17 between them, watched from the bench. Fifth place behind a man who picks like that is a ball-knowledge result, and a lifetime of Arsenal has not taught him to read one.

Antoine Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, the Guardian reports. Edward owns him, and Manchester City, who had been treating him as the natural cover up front, now have one fewer option behind Erling Haaland. BBC Sport says he could miss up to 13 matches.

source.title: Semenyo's eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland

items.text: Justin's Haaland scored twice in Saturday's 3-2 win over Ipswich and hobbled off at full time with a blow to the foot, which makes him a doubt for City's Champions League game against AEK Athens tonight, BBC Sport reports. Maresca said he 'can be available' but the striker was missing from the training session open to the media. If he sits, Maresca has mentioned Foden (Marcus) as a false nine and Ndiaye (Robert) as another option. It is a European tie, so nothing in it counts here.

source.title: Haaland a doubt, Semenyo out - what are Man City's options?

items.text: Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 on Monday night for their first league win of the season, and Justin's Marmoush scored the second with a curling finish, his first goal for the club, BBC Sport reports. James Maddison opened the scoring on his first start in 18 months, Jack Rudoni pulled one back past Marcus's Kinsky, and Ben Davies added the third in stoppage time. Spurs are off the bottom and travel to Chelsea on Saturday, where the league holds Chelsea players on four different squads.

source.title: Spurs 3-1 Coventry: James Maddison shines on Tottenham return

items.text: Small Ben's spare goalkeeper Suzuki scored 8 from the bench while Donnarumma, the one he actually picked, scored 1, and Isak sat next to him on 9. That is two weeks running that the best part of his team has been somewhere he could not see it, and with Small Ben that is usually the explanation: the bench is a shelf, the shelf is high, and he has never once been able to reach the top of it.

Six of Robert's fifteen scored nothing in GW7, Wilson, Estevao, Sesko, Cherki, James and Mosquera among them. It would be a crisis for a man who ever opened the waiver page, and since Robert treats the waiver page the way he treats the group chat, it is a lifestyle. The squad is a museum of purchases from September that nobody has been back to look at.

Edward's Semenyo is out for eight weeks with a knee, and the sad part is that he scored 1 in the last gameweek, so what the league is losing is mostly the idea of a Semenyo. Edward will be along to call it a blow to the squad. It is a blow to a lot of confident messages in the group chat, and the squad barely noticed.

Bruno Fernandes played up front for United, got booked for his trouble and returned 1 point, and Big Ben's other fourteen did exactly what they always do when Bruno does not haul. That is a fifth-place team built on one man's good mood, and on Saturday the mood is a nominal centre-forward again.

Florian Wirtz created nine chances in Liverpool's 2-1 comeback at Brentford, the Guardian reports, and on a night Brentford were down to ten men he finally looked like the No 10 Liverpool paid for. Both of his league assists this season have gone to Victor Munoz, and the one on Saturday was the pass that released Munoz for the equaliser. Big Ben has Wirtz; the Guardian's own line is that he has struggled with the job since joining, so Big Ben may be holding a player who is only now starting to arrive.

source.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend's action

items.text: The chair of the Independent Football Regulator, David Kogan, says it has "absolute power" to force Manchester City's owners to sell if the club is ultimately found to have been run improperly, the Guardian reports. City have appealed the verdict and Kogan would not say whether the IFR will open its own investigation until that is settled, so nothing changes this gameweek. It touches all six of you: City players sit in every squad, Haaland and Gvardiol with Justin, Foden with Marcus, Semenyo with Edward, Ruben with Small Ben, Enzo with Big Ben, Cherki with Robert.

source.title: Football regulator has 'absolute power' to force Manchester City sale if verdict upheld

items.text: Marcus went into GW7 36 clear and came out 19 clear, with Justin's whole squad chewing through the gap while two forwards carried most of his own week. A lead built on two men having a good Saturday gets spent the same way, and GW8 has not even kicked off. Marcus would like you to know that 19 is still a lead.

Robert is 121 behind the leader, with Saka a coin-flip for the weekend and Sesko out with a shin injury and no return date, which means the only thing in his squad moving as slowly as the transfer wire is the one thing leaving at pace: his hairline, which at least has a direction. His title chances are going the same way, minus the dignity of a comb-over.

Bukayo Saka went down after ten minutes of Arsenal's 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich with what Mikel Arteta says 'does not look good at all', a sharp quadriceps pain with nobody near him. Robert owns him and has Saka down as a weekend coin-flip already; Marcus, who also has Arsenal's Tzolis, is told by the BBC that Tzolis is out with a hamstring injury of his own. Eberechi Eze replaced Saka and scored.

source.title: Saka injury 'does not look good' - how will Arsenal cope?

items.text: Declan Rice scored Arsenal's late equaliser at Bayern Munich in a 2-2 draw that the BBC says Arsenal could have won, the one piece of good news for Small Ben out of a night that cost Robert his winger. Eze came on for Saka and scored the opener, and Noni Madueke moved over to the right and looked bright.

source.title: Saka injury 'does not look good' - how will Arsenal cope?

items.text: Bruno Fernandes, Big Ben's, told TNT Sports after Manchester United's 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como that the decision 'from the staff' not to press man to man left too much space behind, and that sometimes 'you have to be more brave'. Michael Carrick answered that if you do not run forward and back 'you aren't going to win'. Marcus has Mbeumo and Robert has Sesko and Yoro in the same dressing room.

source.title: Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation

items.text: Chelsea have conceded one league goal since the international break after letting in a league-high 12 before it, and kept their first clean sheet of the season at Everton on Saturday, with Josh Acheampong a regular in Xabi Alonso's back three. For Robert, who owns Martinez, James and Estevao, and Marcus, who has Joao Pedro, that is the best Chelsea news of the autumn.

source.title: How England hopeful Acheampong is giving Chelsea a big decision to make

items.text: Justin posted the biggest week in the league, 73, with Haaland, Vuskovic and Tavernier all in double figures, and it earned him second place and a view of Marcus's back. It is the most productive way anybody has found of finishing exactly where they started. Next week he gets to do it again, this time with Pickford and Van Hecke gone and a new keeper nobody has heard of.

Big Ben named his team Quantum of Tzolis, which is a fine thing to put on a badge until you look at the squad sheet and find Tzolis at Marcus's, injured, on nothing. Big Ben's best Arsenal contribution of the week was Konsa on 9, with Havertz alongside him on 2, which is about the right amount of ball knowledge for a man who christened his club after somebody else's player.

Edward dropped Semenyo, who is out for eight weeks with a knee, and signed Doku, so the one waiver move of the week doubles as a medical. It was also the right call, and he took it on a night when his own week was 43 with Tarkowski, Gibbs-White and Saliba all on nothing. Nobody who has read the group chat since August will let him call it foresight.

With Bukayo Saka's suspected quad injury leaving Mikel Arteta short of attacking options, the Guardian expects 16-year-old Max Dowman to get his chance on the right at home to Everton on Saturday. He has played only nine Premier League minutes this season. Robert owns Saka, so the wait for a scan result now includes a teenager who is not on any of the six squads taking his shirt.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Ipswich host Nottingham Forest tonight at 8pm BST, and Forest, the league's lowest scorers with five goals in seven games, get Morgan Gibbs-White back after he missed the defeat by Arsenal. Edward owns him. Oliver Glasner called Liam Delap one of his best finishers and wants to get him into better positions, with 12 of Delap's 14 Premier League goals coming for Ipswich, per the Guardian.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Manchester City go to Aston Villa on Saturday at 12.30pm BST needing a win to become just the third side to take maximum points from their first eight Premier League games, according to the Guardian. Villa have recovered from a single point in their first four league games. Justin has Haaland and Gvardiol in the City camp and Edward has Manzambi at Villa, so somebody gets a bad lunchtime.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: The Guardian reckons Michael Carrick will surely follow if Manchester United lose to Bournemouth on Sunday, after Bruno Fernandes accused his manager of tactical failings following the 4-1 loss at Como. Big Ben owns Fernandes, Marcus has Mbeumo, and Justin has Tavernier and Marcus has Evanilson on the Bournemouth side of it.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Ipswich 1-1 Nottingham Forest at Portman Road: Neco Williams put Forest in front after 13 minutes and Julio Enciso levelled four minutes before half-time. Williams is Edward's and Enciso is Small Ben's, so the weekend's only game so far split its points between those two, with nine fixtures and everybody else still to come.

source.title: Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest - Team Stats

items.text: Small Ben is top of the weekend, which is the one table he gets to look down on, and it took Enciso poaching a goal at Portman Road to put him there. He still sits 49 behind Marcus overall, a gap he will study the way he studies everything else: from below.

Edward's Friday peaked in the thirteenth minute, when Neco Williams scored, and Return of the Djedi has been a sequel nobody asked for since. Gibbs-White spent the remaining 77 minutes of his 90 contributing very little, and Edward now waits for Saturday with nine players still to come, which is the threat and the warning in one.

Marcus spent Friday night exactly where luck likes him: on the sofa, 19 clear of Justin, with all eleven of his players yet to touch a ball. Everyone else did the work and he leads the weekend's argument by not having started it.

Robert's season is an exercise in watching things leave: Saka's thigh has no return date, the leader has 142 points on him, and his hairline, the only one of the three that was never coming back anyway, is the one holding up best.

Chelsea host Tottenham at 5.30pm BST without Emiliano Martinez, who the Guardian lists with a jaw problem until 21 November, and Reece James is out with a knee until January. Mike Penders is expected in goal. Robert owns both of them, so his Chelsea corner starts the evening with a stand-in keeper and no right-back.
